statement: (i) Given $\ln a=2$ and $\ln b=-1$, find $\ln(a^{3}b^{2})$. (ii) Solve $3^{2x}-4\cdot 3^{x}+3=0$. (iii) Show that if $2^{x}=3^{y}$ then $\frac{x}{y}=\frac{\ln 3}{\ln 2}$.
solution: (i) $\ln(a^{3}b^{2})=3\ln a+2\ln b=3\cdot2+2(-1)=4$. (ii) Let $u=3^{x}$: $u^{2}-4u+3=0\Rightarrow u=1$ or $3$, so $x=0$ or $1$. (iii) $2^{x}=3^{y}\Rightarrow x\ln 2=y\ln 3\Rightarrow \frac{x}{y}=\frac{\ln 3}{\ln 2}$.
hints: Use log of a product and power.
